string.text: Batı yaylalarının vahşi tepe insanları Dunlendliler, gururlu ve kadim bir halktır. Rohirrim'e düşmanlık besleyen bu halk, gerilla taktikleri ve savaştaki azmiyle bilinir. Güçlü liderler altında birleşerek, haklı olarak kendilerinin olduğuna inandıkları toprakları geri almak ve hayatta kalmak için savaşırlar.

At Lordları olarak bilinen Rohirrim, geniş ova ve yuvarlak tepelerle kaplı Rohan diyarının gururlu ve asil halkıdır. Binici yetenekleri ve askeri güçlerinin temelini oluşturan eşsiz süvarileriyle ünlüdürler. Sıkı bağlarla örülmüş feodal bir toplumda yaşayan Rohirrim'e, onur ve gelenekle topraklarını ve halkını korumakla yükümlü olan bir kral ve sadık bir soylular sınıfı liderlik eder. Şiddetle bağımsız olan bu halk, özgürlüğe her şeyden çok değer verir ve savaşçıları, güçlü atlarının sırtında mızrak, kılıç ve yay kullanmak üzere eğitilmiştir.

Khand Variagları, doğu bozkırlarından gelen acımasız ve savaşçı bir halktır. Atlara hakimiyetleri ve ölümcül savaş arabalarıyla tanınan bu halk, benzersiz ve acımasız bir savaş tarzı getirir. Sauron'la ittifak halinde olan Variaglar, güç ve yağma için savaşarak Orta Dünya'ya korku saçarlar.

Doğulular, Mordor'un ötesindeki uçsuz bucaksız doğu diyarlarından gelen gururlu ve disiplinli bir halktır. Dayanıklılıkları ve savaş ustalıklarıyla ünlü olan bu halk hem çiftçi hem de savaşçıdır; tarımsal gelenekleri şiddetli bir savaş kültürüyle harmanlarlar. Orduları, süslü zırhlara bürünmüş ve ölümcül mızrak ve yaylarla donanmış korkunç süvarileriyle bilinir. Zengin bir zanaatkarlık mirası ve akrabalarına sadakatle, Doğulular altın ve kırmızı renkli canlı sancakları altında düşmanlarının yüreğine korku salarak savaşa yürürler. Sauron'a bağlılıkları onları müthiş bir güç haline getirmiş, gölgesinin altında birleşerek Orta Dünya'daki egemenliklerini genişletmektedirler.

Güney çöllerinin savaşçıları Haradrim, Sauron'la ittifak halindeki vahşi ve dayanıklı bir halktır. Egzotik savaş canavarları ve yetenekli süvarileriyle tanınan bu halk, kızıl sancakları altında savaşa yürür. Gururlu ve geleneklerine derinden bağlı olan Haradrim, çölün vahşetini Orta Dünya'nın savaş alanlarına taşır.

Yayşör Bard'ın torunları Dale Bardingleri, Erebor'un gölgesinde yaşayan gururlu ve çalışkan bir halktır. Yetenekli okçuları ve disiplinli savaşçılarıyla ünlü olan bu halk, gelişen şehirlerini ve kuzeyin ticaret yollarını korur. Güçlü bir topluluk ve onur duygusuyla birleşen Bardingler, topraklarını tehdit eden karanlığa karşı sağlam dururlar.

Erebor'un asil Cüceleri, zanaatkarlıkları, dayanıklılıkları ve gurlarıyla ünlüdürler. Yalnız Dağ'daki salonlarından, eşsiz güzellikte güçlü silahlar ve hazineler yaratırlar. Zırha bürünmüş ve baltalarla silahlanmış olarak, soydaşlarını sarsılmaz cesaretle savunur, miraslarını geri kazanmaya ve ona tehdit oluşturan herkese karşı geleneklerini korumaya çalışırlar.

Son Huzurlu Ev olan Rivendell, Lord Elrond'un yönetiminde bilgelik ve güzelliğin sığınağıdır. Sisli Dağlar'a yerleşmiş olan halkı, Orta Dünya'nın kadim bilgisinin bilge ustaları ve koruyucularıdır. Rivendell Elfleri, karanlığa karşı direnenler için öğüt ve yardım sunarak, umut ve birlik ışığını korurlar.

Kral Thranduil'in yönetimindeki Kara Orman Orman-Elfleri, uçsuz bucaksız ve gizemli ormanın koruyucularıdır. Çeviklikleri ve yay ustalıklarıyla tanınan bu halk, gölgelere karışır ve kesinlik ve zarafetle saldırır. Diyarları güzellik ve tehlikeyle dolu bir yerdir ve savaşçılarının kararlılığı ile krallarının ebedi bilgeliğiyle korunur. Şiddetle bağımsız olan Kara Orman Elfleri, ormanlarını büyüyen karanlığa karşı korumak için savaşırlar.

Altın Orman sakinleri Lothlórien Galadhrim'leri, Leydi Galadriel ve Lord Celeborn tarafından yönetilen ruhani ve asil bir halktır. Okçuluk ve orman savaşının ustaları olarak, büyülü diyarlarını eşsiz bir yetenekle korurlar. Akrabalarına ve vatanlarına bağlılıkları sarsılmaz olup, ince büyüleri Lothlórien'i büyüyen gölgenin ortasında bir umut ve ışık sığınağı olarak korur.

Beyaz Saruman'ın yönetimindeki Isengard orduları, Uruk-hai'ler ve paralı askerlerin müthiş bir gücüdür. Endüstrinin ateşlerinde dövülmüş olan silah ve zırhları yıkım için tasarlanmıştır. Isengard güçleri, fetih ve hakimiyet peşinde acımasız bir verimlilikle savaşa yürür.

Sis kaplı dağlarda ikamet eden Gundabad Orkları, acımasız ve vahşi bir güçtür. Savaş lordlarının yönetiminde, komşu topraklara sonsuz akınlar düzenlerler. Nefret ve zulüm tarafından yönlendirilen bu halk, kuzeye hakim olma arayışında amansızdır.

Deniz akıncıları ve usta denizciler olan Umbar Korsanları, Sauron'la ittifak halindeki acımasız ve kurnaz bir halktır. Hızlı gemileri ve amansız deniz savaşlarıyla tanınan bu halk, Orta Dünya'nın kıyılarına korku salar. Denizcilik miraslarıyla gurur duyan Korsanlar, karanlık ittifakları adına yağma ve talan yaparak denizlerin kaosunu karaya taşırlar.

Ölümcül'ün komutası altındaki Dol Guldur maşaları, karanlık ve uğursuz bir güçtür. Kara Orman'ın bozulmuş ormanı içinde gizlenerek, düşmanlarını zayıflatmak için ihanet ve gölge kullanırlar. Orklar, varglar ve diğer kötü yaratıklar, Orta Dünya'ya korku ve çürümeyi yaymak için ileri yürürler.

Númenorlu sürgünlerin torunları Gondorlular, Orta Dünya'daki İnsanların en büyük krallığının gururlu kâhyalarıdır. Yükselen taş kaleleri ve sarsılmaz cesaretleriyle bilinen Gondor, Mordor'un tehditkâr gölgesine karşı bir umut kalesidir. Cesur piyade, yetenekli okçular ve atlı şövalyelerden oluşan disiplinli orduları, tüm özgür halklar için bir kalkan görevi görür. Asil kâhyalar ve kaptanların yönetimindeki Gondorlular, geleneklerine sıkı sıkıya bağlıdır ve diyarı ile mirasını koruma görevlerinde taviz vermezler.

Azap Dağı'nın gölgesinde dövülmüş Mordor orduları, Kara Lord Sauron'un komutasındaki amansız bir karanlık gücüdür. Orklar, troller ve kötü insanlardan oluşan bu ordu, yanan Göz'ün altında korku ve yıkım saçarak savaşa yürür. Bu lejyonlar, zulmün ve kullukun pençesinde, pürüzlü kılıçlar ve kaba zırhlarla silahlanmıştır. Sauron'un demir iradesiyle bağlı olan Mordor güçleri, tüm Orta Dünya'yı gölgeye boğmayı amaçlayan ölümcül bir dalgadır.

Âbanissa, Harad'ın derin güneyinde, nemli ormanlar ve kadim taş hanedanların diyarıdır. Âbanissa'nın büyük Haneleri korkunç savaş canavarlarına ve disiplinli mızrakçı ordularına kumanda eder; güçleri Sauron'dan başkasına hesap vermez. Hanedan sancakları altında yürürler ve güney topraklarında hem saygı hem de dehşet uyandırırlar.

Shaghâna, Harad'ın doğu ucu olup güneşin kavurduğu bozkırlar ve kadim kalelerin diyarıdır. Dokuz kabile klanı, yemin ve kan bağıyla birbirine bağlı vahşi biniciler ve akıncılardır; karşı çıkmaya cesaret edenlerin kalbine korku salarlar. Taskral'larına ve onun aracılığıyla Sauron'un iradesine cevap verirler.

Shaghâna, Harad'ın doğu ucu, güneşin kavurduğu bozkırlar ve kadim kalelerle dolu bir diyardır. Dokuz kabile klanı, yemin ve kanla bağlı, onlara karşı çıkmaya cesaret edenlerin kalbine korku salan cesur savaşçılardır.

Shaghâna, doğu Harad bozkırlarının azılı kabile halkıdır, amansız akıncılar ve usta atlılar olarak ünlüdürler. Yemin ve klanla bağlı olan bu halk, Taskral'lerine itaat eder ve güneşin kavurduğu kalelerinden Sauron'un karanlık tasarılarına hizmet eder.

Âbanissa, Harad'ın derin güneyinde, nemli ormanlar ve kadim taş hanedanlarının diyarında yer alır. Âbanissa'nın büyük Haneleri, korku salan savaş canavarlarına ve disiplinli savaşçı ordularına kumanda eder; güçleri sadece Sauron'un kendisine karşı sorumludur.

Âbanissa'nın büyük Haneleri, Harad'ın derin güneyine, nemli ormanlar, kadim taş saraylar ve yükselen savaş canavarlarının diyarına hükmediyorlar. Orduları hanedan sancakları altında yürüyor ve güney topraklarında saygı ve dehşet yayıyorlar.

Yılan Muhafızları, Yakın Harad'ın Yılan Lordu'nun hizmetindeki atlı askerlerdir. Ephel Dúath'ın güneyindeki engebeli ovalarda eyerde yetişen bu savaşçılar, Orta Dünya'nın güney topraklarında ok atıcı süvariler olarak eşsizdir. Harad ve Mordor arasında barış zamanlarında Muhafızlar hizmetlerini Haradrimli lordlara ve altın ücretlerini ödeyebilecek zenginlikte olan diğer güçlere kiralayabilir.

Gri Takım, çağlar önce krallıklarını kaybetmiş Arnor krallarının soyundan gelen Dúnedain Korucularının son örgütlü kardeşliğidir. Kendi yurtları olmadan Kuzey'de at sürerler, isimlerini unutmuş topraklarda barışı korurlar. İlk sadakatleri Elendil soyuna olsa da, gezginlikleri onları medeni topraklara getirdiğinde Orta Dünya'nın dört bir yanındaki lordlardan sözleşmeler alırlar.

Erebor Baltacıları, barış zamanının mizaçlarına uymadığını keşfeden Kral Thorin'in savaşlarının gazileridir. Cüce salonlarının yakın çarpışma tekniklerinde eğitilmiş olan bu savaşçılar — kalkan duvarı, kısa balta, kazma — her arazide müthiştirler ama Erebor'u insanların krallıklarına bağlayan dağ geçitlerinde parlarlar. Ücretlerini ödeyebilecek herkesten sözleşme alırlar, ancak Erebor veya Rivendell'e karşı balta kaldırmazlar.

Korsan Kılıçları, Umbar limanlarından gelen ve becerilerini karada satmaya başlayan gazi deniz savaşçılarıdır. Gemi savaşının tercih edilen silahı olan tatar olarak savaşırlar ve bir kuşatmada dalgalanan bir güverte üzerindeki kadar rahattırlar. Yüzü yara izli Númenórlı sürgün kaptanları, itibarlarının en değerli yükleri olduğunu bilerek onları demir bir disiplinle sözleşmelerine bağlı tutar.

Kör Göz, Harad kıyıları ve derin çöl boyunca faaliyet gösteren kaçakçılardan, malı götürenlerden ve kiralık katillerden oluşan bir kardeşliktir. Unutulmuş bir Haradrimli krala hizmet eden bir suikastçı tarikatından geldikleri söylenir ve yöntemleri — zehir, gölge ve sırları kullanma — değişmeden kalmıştır. Bir rakibini sessizce ortadan kaldırmak isteyen lordlar veya gümrük denetimi olmadan yük taşınması gereken tüccarlar, bir altın sikke ve mühürlü bir mektubun nereye bırakılacağını bilir.

Variag Yağmacıları, Khand bozkırlarından gelen genç Variag savaşçılarının ritüel savaş halinde erken yetişkinliklerini geçiren savaş çeteleridir: pişmiş yiyecek sahibi olamazlar, kalıcı çatı altında uyuyamazlar ve merhamet gösteremezler. Çoğu sonunda klanlarının yerleşik yaşamına geri dönse de, bazıları hiç dönmez ve bunlar Yağmacıları oluşturur — Khand yollarını yağmalayan ve sınırlarını aşarak Harad ve Gondor'a baskınlar düzenleyen kanun kaçakları.

Dunlending Akıncıları, bir zamanlar şimdi Rohirrim'in yönettiği vadilerde yaşayan bir tepe klanının kırık kalıntısıdır. Büyükbabaları verimli topraklardan kayalık yüksekliklere sürüldü ve onlar bu acıyı bir akıncı felsefesine dönüştürdü: bir güneyden veya kralın adamından alınan her şey yalnızca çalınanın iadesiydi. Pratikte eşkıyadırlar, ama tepelerdeki her keçi yolunu bilen tehlikeli eşkıyalardır.

Ağız'ın Hizmetkârları, Kara Kapı'nın ötesinde faaliyet gösteren Barad-dûr'un Gözleridir — Mordor'a komşu halklar arasına sızmış muhbirler, tetikçiler ve casuslar. Sauron'un orduları henüz ulaşamadığı yerlerde, bu ajanlar haraç toplar ve muhalefeti susturur. Rüşvet, şantaj ve sessiz cinayetlerle çalışırlar, Karanlık Efendi'ye karşı hiçbir komployu kök salmadan söküp yok etmek için.

Uzun Göl'ün Yağmacıları, Esgaroth'un saygın ışıklarından uzakta, Uzun Göl'ün gölgeli kıyılarındaki kamışlıklarda ve çürümüş eski iskelelerde yaşarlar. Geçimlerini sahte fenerlerle mavnaları gizli sığlıklara çekerek, ardından yükü soyup kasabanın içindeki aracılar vasıtasıyla satarak sağlarlar. Göl-kasabası Efendisi ve Dale tüccarlarının çabalarına rağmen, Yağmacıların rıhtım tavernalarında o kadar çok dostu vardır ki kolayca kovulamazlar.

Göz Kapaksız Tarikatı, Kara Númenor geleneğine dayanan gizli bir topluluktur ve Sauron'u yeniden yükseldiğinde sadık kullarını ihtişama kavuşturacak bir tanrı-kral olarak tapar. Dunland'ın mülksüzleri ve diyarın unutulmuş köşeleri arasında üye toplarlar, ilahi lütuf ve dünyevi güç vaat ederler. Gerçekte liderleri Barad-dûr'un ajanlarına hesap verir ve hücre tabanlı yapıları onları herhangi bir lordun adaleti için neredeyse yok edilemez kılar.

Kum-Binicileri, derin Harad içlerinin göçebe çöl klanlarıdır, Ephel Dúath ile uzak güney denizi arasındaki susuz çöllerin efendileridir. Sadece kendilerinin bildiği yollar boyunca dolaşırlar, topraklarından geçmeye cüret eden her kervan kuşağından haraç alırlar. Yakın Harad'ın yerleşik lordları onları baş belası olarak görür; Kum-Binicileri ise yerleşik lordları çölün zaten özgürce verdiğini çalan hırsızlar sayar.

Vahşi Doğulular, Rhûn Denizi'nin fethedilmemiş bozkır klanlarıdır, onları dizginlemeye çalışan her lordun otoritesine — Rhûn reisi, Mordor teğmeni ve Dale Kralı fark etmez — karşı durmuşlardır. Celduin'in doğusundaki otlaklarda dolaşırlar, at toplar, sürüleri yağmalar ve silahlı bir koruma olmadan bozkırlarını geçmeye cüret eden her kervan kuşağından yol haracı alırlar.

İnsanlarca Wose veya Ormanların Vahşi İnsanları olarak bilinen Drúedain, Drúadan'ın derin ormanlarında ve Beyaz Dağlar'ın gizli vadilerinde yaşayan kadim bir halktır. Ateşle toprak temizler, kül açısından zengin toprakta ihtiyaçlarını yetiştirirler ve toprak tükendiğinde göç ederler — Orta Dünya'nın yerleşik halkalarının asla anlamadığı ve anlamaya tenezzül etmediği bir yaşam tarzı. Drúedain lord istemez, vergi ödemez ve yalnızca ormanın sessizliğinde bırakılmayı ister.

Beorningler, Sisli Dağlar ile Mirkwood arasında Anduin vadisinde yaşayan büyük ormancılardır, Beorn soyunun deri-değiştiricileri tarafından yönetilirler. Topraklarından hiçbir Ork geçmesine izin vermezler, nöbetlerini finanse etmek için Carrock Geçidi'nde haraç alırlar ve Orta Dünya'da hiçbir krala hesap vermezler. Elfler ve Cücelerle ticaret yapar ve konuşsalar da, izinsiz ormanlarından geçmeye cüret eden herhangi bir ordu Beorninglerin çok büyük dişlere sahip olduğunu keşfeder.

Dorwinion İnsanları, Rhûn Denizi'nin üzerindeki ılık yamaçlarda bağlara bakar ve şarapları Kızılsu ile Akarsu boyunca çok uzaklardaki Elflerin ve İnsanların salonlarına ulaşır. Onlar bağcı, kayıkçı ve nehir tüccarıdır; bir yabancıyla dövüşmektense ona mal satmayı yeğleyen bir Kuzeyli halktır. Kralları sarayını Vineholm'de tutar ve her yıl iç denizin ötesindeki Doğulular, onun zengin ve az korunan topraklarına daha bir dikkatle bakar.

Güney Rhovanion'un Kuzeylileri, Karanlık Orman'ın güney eteği ile Kahverengi Topraklar arasındaki geniş ovalarda at sürer; kuzeydeki Éothéod'u akraba sayan, özgür bir at yetiştiricisi halktır. İki kez Araba Sürenler arabaları ve ateşleriyle Doğu'dan gelip onları kırdı; ovaların atlıları bunu unutmadı.

Efsane metinleri ve bazı sahnelerdeki örümcek ağları kalır. Varsayılan: kapalı.

Etkinken (varsayılan), lordlar savaşta kendi taraflarına bağlı kalır. Özgür Halkların bir YZ klanı asla bir Kötü diyara katılmaz, kaçmaz veya paralı asker olarak hizmet etmez; bir Kötü klan da asla bunu bir Özgür diyar için yapmaz. Tarafsız klanlar ve diyarlar her iki tarafla da iş yapabilir. Yeni bir sefer ayrıca Özgür ve Kötü lordlar arasında hiç dostluk olmadan başlar: her biri aynı güçte düşmanlığa dönüşür. Kendi klanınız ve liderlik ettiğiniz bir diyar temel oyunun kurallarına uyar. Karşı tarafın bir diyarına zaten hizmet eden klanlar oldukları yerde kalır. Kapalıyken temel oyunun kuralları geçerlidir. Hemen uygulanır, yeniden başlatma gerekmez; dostluk kısmı yalnızca yeni seferler için geçerlidir.

Açıkken, Tarafsız bir diyar Yüzük Savaşı'na temelli katılabilir. Tam Savaş'ta, savaş göstergesinde çok geride kalan taraf (25 puan veya daha fazla) kendi yönüne meyilli Tarafsız bir diyara çağrı yapar: Khand, Rhudaur, Umbar, Shaghana ve Abanissa Gölge'ye; Cardolan ve Dorwinion Özgür Halklara meyillidir. Diyar sonra karşı tarafın her diyarıyla savaşa girer ve bu savaş Yüzük Savaşı sürdükçe barışla sona eremez. Bir seferde tek diyar katılır, war_pledge.json aksini söylemedikçe 30 gün arayla ve asla bir oyuncunun yönettiği diyar değil. Momentum Takibi açık olmalıdır. Kapalı olması YZ'nin yeni katılımlarını durdurur; katılmış bir diyar katılmış kalır. Varsayılan: açık.
Seçkin Birlikler Yalnızca Altına Mal Olsun açıkken, elçinin altın fiyatı birliğin temel elçi maliyetinin bu sayıyla çarpımıdır. Kaynak fiyatı da aynı temel maliyetin bir katıdır. Varsayılan: 200.

Bir unvan üzerinde hak iddiası satın almanın bedeli; realms_titles.xml içindeki fiyatının yüzdesi olarak (Baronluk için 40'tan Krallık için 500'e dek, halkınızın kendi kaynağıyla). YZ lordları kendilerininkini altınla, aynı yüzdeden öder. 10 ile 500 arası. Varsayılan: 100.

Bir unvanı gasbetmenin, kurmanın, yeniden tesis etmenin veya geri almanın nüfuz maliyeti; realms_titles.xml içindeki maliyetinin yüzdesi olarak. Gondor'un tahtını Aragorn için yeniden tesis etmek 100'de 2500'e mal olur. YZ lordları için de geçerlidir. 10 ile 500 arası. Varsayılan: 100.

Açıkken, YZ lordları her hafta hak iddiası satın alır, iddia ettikleri unvanları gasbeder, kendi taraflarının elindeki boş unvanları kurar ve tahtları yeniden tesis eder. Kapalıyken yalnızca siz yaparsınız; hâlihazırda sahip oldukları iddialar kalır. Varsayılan: açık.

Açıkken, diyarınızda lordları klanınızınkinin hemen altındaki unvanlara sahip olan her klan, klanınıza tımarlarından elde ettiği günlük gelirin bir payını öder. Beklenen altın değişiminde görünür. YZ lordları için de geçerlidir. Alma ve ödeme ayrıdır: yalnızca bu açıkken, efendiler altını kazanır ama vasalları kaybetmez. Varsayılan: açık.
Bir vasal klanın tımarlarından elde ettiği günlük gelirin, efendi klanına giden payı. Birden fazla efendi klanı olan bir klan bunu aralarında böler. 1 ile 25 arası. Varsayılan: 5.

Açıkken, klanınız her efendi klana, yani diyarınızda lordu sizinkilerden birinin hemen üstündeki bir unvana sahip olan klana, tımarlarından elde ettiği günlük gelirin bir payını öder. Beklenen altın değişiminde görünür. YZ lordları için de geçerlidir. Haracının tamamını ödeyemeyen bir klan o gün hiçbir şey ödemez. Yalnızca bu açıkken, vasallar altını kaybeder ama efendileri kazanmaz. Varsayılan: açık.
Bir klanın tımarlarından elde ettiği günlük gelirin efendi klanlarına ödediği pay; birden fazlası varsa aralarında bölünür. 1 ile 25 arası. Varsayılan: 5.
Gondor Kâhyası veya Mark Mareşali gibi bir makamın sahibinin klanına her hafta ödediği nüfuz; realms_titles.xml içindeki miktarının yüzdesi olarak. 0 bunu durdurur. 0 ile 300 arası. Varsayılan: 100.
Açıkken, başka bir klanın sahip olduğu bir şehrin veya kalenin unvanını taşıyan bir lord, her hafta o yerin sahibinden biraz daha az hoşlanır ve şehir biraz sadakat kaybeder. Varsayılan: açık.
Açıkken, başka bir hanedanın vasalı, efendilik unvanının sahibini her hafta biraz daha sever; en fazla 30 ilişkiye kadar. Varsayılan: açık.
Açıkken, bir vasalı orduya çağırmak efendisine nüfuzun yarısına mal olur. Kapalıyken, temel oyunun istediği kadar olur. Varsayılan: açık.

Açıkken, YZ lordları yetişkin çocuklarına küçük unvanlar verir. Kapalıyken onları kendilerinde tutarlar; daha önce devredilmiş unvanlar kalır, ayrıca sefer başlangıcında yapılan bağışlar da kalır, örneğin Boromir'in Batı Osgiliath'ı. Varsayılan: açık.

Açıkken, lord birlikleri ve konuşmaların üstündeki isim lordun hitabını ve unvanını taşır, örneğin Gondor Kâhyası Denethor. Kapalıyken yalnızca sade ismi gösterirler; ansiklopedi yine de tüm unvanları listeler. Birlik isimleri oyun içi bir saat içinde değişir. Varsayılan: açık.

Yalnızca yuvarlak savaş HUD'undaki üç halkayı değiştirir: oyuncu canın, binek canın ve kalkanın. Varsayılan, onların taş görünümünü ve renklerini korur. Diğer her seçenek, bu halkaları koyu bir zemin üzerinde, o renk görüşü türü için birbirinden ayırt edilmesi daha kolay düz renklerle çizer. Halkalar eskisi gibi sıralarını ve dolumlarını korur, böylece yerleri ve uzunlukları da onları ayırt etmeyi sağlar. Kariyer yeteneği merkezi, cephane sayısı ve diğer tüm ekranlar değişmez. Değişiklik, yeniden başlatmaya gerek kalmadan mevcut savaşta geçerli olur.

Adı anılan kahramanlar, yakınlarındaki müttefik askerleri her biri kendi yöntemiyle güçlendirir: Dain'in cüceleri ayakta kalır, Aragorn'un adamları soğukkanlılığını korur, elf lordlarının okçuları daha hızlı yay gerer. Yalnızca hero_auras.json dosyasında listelenen kahramanlar bir aura taşır. Bir aura ile bir askerin kendi ırk yeteneği aynı şeyi verdiğinde, güçlü olan geçerlidir; asla toplanmazlar. Bir sonraki aura nabzından itibaren etkili olur.

Her auranın bonuslarını çarpar. 1.0, hero_auras.json dosyasında yazıldığı gibidir; 0 tüm auraları kapatır. Moral alt sınırları ve darbeyi savuşturma gibi açık/kapalı etkiler ölçeklenmez. Varsayılan: 1.0.

When enabled (default), the towns and castles of a sworn enemy realm treat you as they would in war, even while your realms are at peace: you enter a town only in disguise, a castle not at all, and you cannot trade, recruit or rest in its villages. No Trade Agreements With Enemy Realms

When enabled (default), a Free realm and a realm of the Shadow never sign a trade agreement, neither by the AI nor by your own kingdom's vote. An agreement signed before this was switched on runs to its end. When off, the base game's rules apply. Applies at once, no restart.
No Caravan Trade With Enemy Realms

When enabled (default), caravans of a Free realm do not trade in the towns of a realm of the Shadow, and the reverse, while the two are at peace before the War of the Ring. Realms that are not sworn enemies trade as before. When off, the base game's rules apply. Applies at once, no restart.

When off (default), a kingdom you rule cannot ally with a realm on the other side of the war: a Free kingdom does not ally with the Shadow, and the reverse. AI realms keep their own rules either way. Applies at once, no restart. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

Leave ON while diagnosing the intermittent battle-load hang — the LAST line in the log names the stuck phase / agent.

If a mission exit stalls past 15s, briefly suspends the game's main thread (at +15/+30/+60s) to photograph its call stack into the TAOM debug log — this is what root-caused the tournament-exit freeze (#331). Tiny residual risk: a suspension landing mid-GC can freeze the game harder than the stall itself. Turn OFF to keep the other diagnostics without any thread suspension. Default ON.

If a battle frame stops for 10s (the agent AI tick or the main mission frame never finishes: the game freezes with no crash), briefly suspends the stuck thread at +10/+20/+40s to photograph its call stack into the TAOM debug log as [MissionStall]. It never runs while the game is responsive, and never while a mission is ending or exiting (the exit sampler above covers that). Independent of the master Battle Load Diagnostics toggle: this is crash forensics, not load logging. Same tiny residual risk as the exit sampler. Default ON.

Writes memory telemetry to the TAOM debug log: a periodic [MemSample] line (process private/working-set MB, managed heap, system commit use/limit, available RAM), a one-shot WARN when system commit headroom runs low, and a [MemStation] line each time a screen opens or closes so growth can be attributed to a screen. This ONE switch governs all three. Independent of the master Battle Load Diagnostics toggle: this is session-wide crash forensics, not battle-load phase logging. Default ON.
Seconds between [MemSample] lines. Default 30s (~120 lines per hour of play). Takes effect on the next sample — no restart needed.

Writes a [MissionPerf] line to the TAOM debug log every 5 seconds while a mission runs: frames, fps, average / p95 / max frame time in ms, agent and formation counts, garbage collections, and the engine's main-thread and render-thread busy times (mainMs, renderMs). This is the in-mission counterpart of [MemSample] and the measurement an AI or content change is judged against. Cost is one timestamp and one GetMainFps read per frame. Default ON.

Off by default. Adds per-type attribution to the hitch probe's lines: times every mission behaviour's tick, every behaviour's spawn callback and every scene script component by type, and lists the slowest. Installed once at game start: turning it on takes effect after a restart; turning it off stops it from the next mission.

How many entries each [TickProfile] and [TickSummary] line lists (mission behaviours) and each [MapProfile] and [MapProfileSummary] line lists (map tick listeners and TAOM map views), slowest first. Default 8. Read at each mission start and each campaign session start.

A frame that takes this many milliseconds or more writes one [Hitch] line naming where the frame went, for the first 100 such frames of a mission; later ones are only counted. Below the battle's usual frame time, nearly every frame is a hitch. Default 250. Read at each mission start.

On by default. Times the parts of every mission frame TAOM can see (the wait for the agent tick, the mission tick, the camera and render preparation, scene scripts, agent spawns) and checks whether an animation clip is loading from disk, so each frame slower than the hitch threshold writes a hitch line and a detail line saying where the time went. Its measured cost is written to the TAOM debug log. Installed once at game start: turning it on takes effect after a restart; turning it off stops measuring from the next mission while 'Enable Tick Profiler' is off (the profiler measures through the probe's patches).

Writes an [AnimMem] line to the TAOM debug log every 5 seconds while a mission runs: how much on-demand animation clip data the engine holds against its 12 MiB budget, whether a clip is loading from disk at the moment of a sample, and how often the total fell between one-second samples (a sign that clips were evicted), plus a summary when the mission ends. Read-only: it finds the two engine values once per game session by a signature check, then once a second reads the clip byte total and asks the engine whether a clip is loading; if the check fails on this game version it turns itself off and says why in the log. Takes effect at the next mission start. Default ON.

Off by default. Times the campaign map's frame: the campaign tick, every per-frame tick-event listener by its owner, the map screen and TAOM's map views, and TAOM's application tick. Writes a [MapProfile] line to the TAOM debug log every 5 seconds while the map runs and a [MapProfileSummary] line when the campaign ends. Turning it on takes effect after a restart (the profiler is installed once, at game start); turning it off stops measuring from the next campaign session.

The campaign map updates every settlement nameplate every frame (about a thousand in TAOM), hidden ones included. When on, a nameplate that is hidden and cannot become visible this frame (out of height range, not tracked, not in range, nothing about its settlement changed) is left alone, which saves frame time on the map, most in fast forward. Everything else updates exactly as in the vanilla game. Takes effect on the next frame, so it can be switched with the map profiler on to compare the [MapProfile] lines. Default ON.

In the measurement this feature is adapted from, every screen or menu that covered the campaign map left three colour targets and one depth target of the map view's old set behind (tens of megabytes of graphics memory per closed screen, more at a high resolution). That memory stays until a battle, or a town, village or arena scene, starts. When on, every Nth cover (see Map View Release Interval) has the map view release its graphics memory as you return to the map. The map then shows a short loading screen until its view is ready again, on one return in N (about 0.4 s instead of 0.08 s in that measurement). Takes effect at the next cover. Default ON.

Release the map view's memory on every Nth cover of the map. Default 20. A lower number gives memory back sooner but shows the short loading screen on more returns to the map (about 0.4 s in the measurement this feature is adapted from); 1 releases on every cover. Takes effect at the next cover.

Writes the detailed load-time lines to the TAOM debug log: one [PatchApply] line per Harmony patch group with its apply time (written at game initialization), [LoadPhase] steps of TAOM's game start and game initialization, and [Lifecycle] lines timing every campaign handler of a new game, a loaded save and the session start (a line for each handler taking 10 ms or more, and a total per event). The per-type [LoadXml] lines, the patch phase totals and one [Lifecycle] dispatch line per campaign dispatch are always written. Costs a few microseconds per handler while a campaign loads and nothing during play. Default OFF.
Writes one [ScreenOpen] line per screen open to taom_debug.log, naming the screen, the phase and the milliseconds it took. Use it to compare a Fast Open switch off against on. Default OFF.
Opens the Clan screen faster by building its parties list once instead of three times. Turning it off restores vanilla's build for this screen. Read on every open. Default ON.
Opens the Inventory and trade screen faster by skipping work the screen repeats. Turning it off restores vanilla's build for this screen. Read on every open. Default ON.
Opens the Party screen faster by caching lookups the screen repeats for each troop. Turning it off restores vanilla's build for this screen. Read on every open. Default ON.
Opens the Quest log faster by building finished quests only when you select them. Turning it off restores vanilla's build for this screen. Read on every open. Default ON.

Turn ON only to reproduce a combat or siege crash. Logs every damaging blow, every death, and every siege-engine shot to the TAOM debug log (Logs/taom_debug_*.log) with durable flushing, so the LAST line survives a hard native crash and names the fatal blow — victim race, blow flags, damage type, whether it was a fire pot. Costs a synchronous log write per hit while ON, so leave OFF for normal play. Default OFF.

Master toggle. When off, every TAOM crash finalizer passes exceptions straight through and the AppDomain hook ignores them, so the game's own handler takes over (BUTR's too, unless TAOM already suspended it this session; then restart). Takes effect immediately: the finalizers are always installed at launch and check this toggle only when an exception arrives. Default ON.
On first capture, calls ButterLib.ExceptionHandlerSubSystem.Disable() so TAOM's report wins. Default ON.

Logs and survives exceptions thrown inside a short list of native-to-managed callbacks (screen early, late and input ticks, scene-script ticks, thumbnail and tableau rendering, and mission combat callbacks for hits, blocks, missiles, charges, falls and agent removal) instead of crashing. When off, those exceptions pass straight through. Takes effect immediately. Default ON.

When a mission behavior, a module's mission-start callback or a mission object throws in one of the six start calls of Mission.AfterStart while a mission is loading, log it, show a short message, cut that call short and let the mission start, instead of the game loading the mission again every frame for ever. A throw elsewhere in the load, such as a behavior's OnMissionScreenPreLoad, is not covered. Enable Crash Capture does not affect this setting. When off, the exception passes straight through as in the vanilla game. Takes effect immediately. Default ON.

The engine reserves room for the skeletons drawn in each frame in two per-frame buffers (65,536 and 262,144 entries) and never checks that the next one fits; one skeleton too many (about 2,340 in view for the first buffer) freezes the battle for good. When on, TAOM bounds-checks both buffers by rewriting 13 bytes of the engine at launch at each one, so a skeleton that would not fit is drawn from that buffer's first slots instead (its bones may look wrong for that frame). TAOM installs each check only where the exact engine bytes are found exactly once: a build that only moves the function is still patched, and a changed build gets nothing written. It also writes nothing for a buffer another module already guards, and guards the other one regardless. Takes effect at the next launch. Default ON.

Reads how full those two buffers get during every mission, not only battles, and writes the peaks to the log when the mission ends, with how many times each guard had to step in. If nothing guards the first buffer, also shows one warning at 90 percent full. Takes effect at the start of the next mission. Default ON.
Produces Logs/taom_crash_<timestamp>_<sig>.zip containing report.txt, report.json, taom_debug.log, rgl_log.txt, manifest.txt. Default ON.

Writes one zip in the Logs folder with what a bug report needs: this game's and the previous game's TAOM logs, the game's own logs, the game's crash folder from the previous game (files up to 64 MB each, 128 MB in all), the module list, the TAOM settings and, in a campaign, the campaign details. Then shows where the zip is. It carries your PC's name, your hero's name and folder paths of your install.
Offer A Bug Report After An Unexpected End

On the first main menu after a game that closed without TAOM's normal shutdown (a crash, a freeze you had to close, or a stopped game), ask whether to make a bug report from that game's logs. Default ON.
QA only. Throws a tagged TaomDevTriggerException on the next Mission.Tick to exercise the crash capture pipeline. Auto-resets to OFF after firing.
QA only. Throws a tagged TaomDevTriggerException on the next Module.OnApplicationTick to exercise the capture pipeline without entering a mission. Auto-resets to OFF after firing.

QA only. Throws a tagged TaomDevTriggerException from a TAOM mission behavior's AfterStart on the next mission start, the #699 shape. Needs Enable Crash Capture on. With Survive Mission Start Failures on, the mission starts with that behavior's AfterStart cut short, and one message shows. With it off, the throw escapes once, TAOM's crash capture shows its crash dialog and writes a bundle, and the engine loads the mission again. Auto-resets to OFF after firing.
Reveals all characters in the encyclopedia, including those not yet encountered. Equivalent to the 'campaign.toggle_information_restrictions' cheat.

Weighted party size: elite units consume more party capacity. Elites 2x, level 41+ elites 3x, warg riders 2x, cave trolls 4x, mumakil 10x. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

Lets AI lord parties HOLD the roster their party template spawns them with. Without this they spawn at 500-3000 and are trimmed back to the vanilla 50-150 cap within a day. Also relieves AI food and wage pressure, because those drive a second, morale-based desertion path that ignores the cap entirely. Off restores the pre-feature behaviour. Note that is not the same as raw vanilla: the Troop Weight elite tax has its own toggle and still deflates a heavy party's limit when it is on. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

Multiplies an AI lord's party size limit. Preserves clan-tier progression, so a tier-4 lord still outgrows a tier-1. 1.0 = vanilla, which is the default: this feature ships neutral and you opt in. Raise this and the Flat Bonus together: the bonus is added after the multiplier, so moving one alone shifts the total by less than you expect. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
AI Lord Party Size Flat Bonus

Added to an AI lord's party size limit AFTER the multiplier, so it is worth exactly this many men. Exists because template spawn size does not scale with clan tier: under a multiplier alone, low-tier lords still shed. Default: 0. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Multiplies every settlement garrison's size limit, player-owned included. Siege balance, not an AI handicap: lords fielding thousands would walk over garrisons still capped near vanilla's 200. Raising this also gives lords more room to donate troops on entering a friendly fief. 1.0 = vanilla, which is the default. IMPORTANT: raise this only alongside the AI Lord multiplier above. Vanilla refuses to even target a settlement when the attacker is under twice the defender's strength, and that strength counts garrison AND militia, so a high garrison multiplier with vanilla-sized lord parties stops AI sieges happening at all. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Fraction of an AI lord party's food consumption waived. A large party cannot buy 30 days of food from any town, so it starves permanently, and starvation is -30 morale which opens vanilla's morale-desertion path. 0 = vanilla, which is the default. Only worth raising if you have raised the AI Lord multiplier: at vanilla party sizes nothing starves. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Fraction of an AI lord party's wage bill waived. AI clan wage budgets are set from clan gold and a large party blows past them, pinning unpaid wages at -20 morale and opening the same desertion path. 0 = vanilla, which is the default. Only worth raising if you have raised the AI Lord multiplier. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
Apply Party Size To Player Clan

Whether YOUR clan's lord parties get the same size scaling as AI lords. 'Taken-over lords only' (default) applies it when you started as an existing lord via Player Switcher, whose clan was given AI-sized rosters at world generation and would otherwise shed thousands of men. Detected from the player clan's id, so it survives save/load. 'Always' also applies it to an ordinary campaign start. 'Never' is the pre-2026-09-01 behaviour. Food and wage relief are never granted to your clan either way.

Corrects garrison food consumption (Troop Weight no longer inflates it for elite garrisons) and applies the tunable food knobs in settlement_food/settlement_food_config.json (consumption divisors, base/village/flat production, storage caps). Off = vanilla engine food math (garrison food stays weighted). Config edits need an app restart.

Regenerates town market gold toward a higher target (base 25000 vs vanilla 10000) so drained town markets recover — tunable in settlement_economy/settlement_economy_config.json (base, gold per prosperity, daily regen rate). Applies to existing saves immediately. Off = vanilla engine gold math. Config edits need an app restart.

Makes AI/player caravans range beyond the local town cluster instead of shuttling between very-close towns, trade across the endless Free-vs-Evil war (per War Trade Policy below), and carry fuller baskets. Off = exact vanilla caravan behavior. Advanced curve knobs live in caravan_trade/caravan_trade_config.json; config edits need an app restart.

When on, your OWN caravans also range further, trade cross-war, and buy fuller baskets (they may enter contested territory and risk attack). Off scopes the selection re-weight + basket diversity off your clan's caravans. Note: the wider distance ceiling is engine-global (shared by all caravans) and the war-trade gate scopes at your whole faction, so those two levers aren't fully isolated to non-player caravans — but with this off your caravans still route by vanilla's nearest-first selection.
How much further caravans range past the vanilla distance ceiling. 1.0 = vanilla reach; higher = they visit more distant, more profitable markets. Default: 1.6.

Which towns caravans may trade with despite the war. Vanilla = war blocks trade (the cause of the shuttle). Same Side + Neutral = trade with same-alignment or neutral factions but not the enemy side (default, lore-friendly). Ignore War = trade anywhere non-besieged.
Raises poor caravans' buying power so they stock several goods instead of one. 0 = vanilla (poor caravans buy a single item); higher = fuller baskets. Default: 0.35.
When enabled, castles gain notables with recruitable volunteers — the player can 'Recruit troops' at any accessible castle. Existing notables remain in the save if you later disable this.
When enabled, AI lord parties also score, travel to, and recruit volunteers from castles like they do from towns. Requires Enable Castle Recruitment.
How many recruiters each castle is populated with (vanilla towns = 5, villages = 3). Higher = more recruitment volume per castle. Default: 3.

At a faction's key settlements (capitals), speak with the faction emissary to buy that faction's elite troops for its special resource (Castar, War Spoils, Gems...). Conquering a settlement flips its offerings to the new owner.
When on, the emissary option is hidden at settlements whose owner faction has no special resource. When off, the option still appears but is disabled with an explanatory hint.

The most you may bet in each tournament round. 0 = unlimited (up to your purse); raise this slider for a bigger cap, or back to 0 to remove it. Roguery's Deep Pockets doubles any other value. Vanilla is 150. Default: 15,000. Saved values from before 2026-11-10 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
Scales the renown a tournament winner earns (base: vanilla's 3 plus 1 per lord or hero in the field, times the winner's culture factor). 1.00 = as designed. Applies to every winner. Default: 1.00.

Scales the influence a tournament winner earns in a town of their own kingdom (base: 2 plus 1 per 4 lords or heroes in the field, times the winner's culture factor). 1.00 = as designed. Default: 1.00.

A Free People's tournament seats no lord, wanderer or troop of the Shadow, and a tournament of the Shadow seats none of the Free Peoples; each is replaced by one of the town's own troops. A town's side is its owner's, so a captured town follows its conqueror, and a town held by a neutral realm bars nobody. Neutral lords and wanderers, the troops the town itself recruits, you and your clan always compete. Fewer lords in the field means a lesser prize. Default: on.

Adds an option to a town's arena menu: for a small fee the arena master names the nearest towns holding a tournament now that are not at war with your realm. It marks nothing on the map. When off, the option is hidden. Single-player only. Default: on.

Markets and battle loot hand out light and medium armour freely. Heavy, elite and lord pieces are sold only where a town's armoury, its Barracks, is high enough; lord kit can also be forged there or earned piece by piece on the lord's gear ladder, whose last rung awards the named hero weapons; they are never sold or looted. Visit a town's armoury to upgrade a piece with metals. Takes effect from the next game load.
After a battle your side wins against an enemy lord, you may rarely find his household's lord harness among the spoils. Needs Armour Acquisition on.
Now and then a master armourer visits a town for a week, raising its armoury one level. Needs Armour Acquisition on.

When enabled, a town/castle (and its villages) conquered by a different culture gradually adopts the new owner's culture — producing their troops, militia, and identity. Disabling stops NEW conversions; already-converted settlements stay converted.
Days the new owner must hold a cross-culture fief before it converts. Lower = faster cultural takeover. Default: 1 (near-instant on capture).
When enabled, a conquered fief only converts once its loyalty is high enough (configured in culture_conversion_config.json), so a city in unrest never flips. Default: off.

When enabled, conversion also replaces the settlement's notables with ones of the new culture (a Mordor-held Gondor town gets orc notables). Their workshops, alleys and caravans transfer to the newcomers; your relations with the old notables do not. Default: on.

When enabled, conversion re-mans the fief's garrison with the new culture's troops, matching tier, battlefield role and head count (a Gondor tier-4 archer becomes a Mordor tier-4 archer). Without this a fief taken by gift, barter or a king's decision keeps its old culture's garrison forever. Default: on.

When enabled, conversion also swaps the settlement's and its villages' existing militia to the new culture's militia troops. New militia already spawn in the new culture once the fief converts; this makes the standing militia catch up the same day instead of over many. Default: on.
Replace Garrison In Your Own Fiefs
When disabled, the two swaps above never touch a fief your clan owns, so a garrison you stacked by hand survives the conversion. AI fiefs still swap, and your fief still changes culture. Default: on.

When enabled, a scripted war will escalate between Free Peoples and Dark Powers. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

Days after campaign start when Isengard and Dunland attack Rohan. Default 30. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.

Days after campaign start when all hostile kingdoms go to war and peace between hostile tiers is blocked. Default 44. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.
Uses the short delays from war_of_the_ring.json (1/3 days) for rapid testing. Overrides Phase 1/2 days.

Tracks Evil vs Good war progress from battles, sieges, raids, armies and relative strength. The war ends at the victory threshold only when Enable Victory (End the War) is on; that setting is off by default, so the war is endless. Default: on.
Shows the on-map War of the Ring slider once the full war begins. Click it for the detailed breakdown. Default: on.

When OFF (default) the War of the Ring is endless: momentum is tracked but no side ever wins. Turn ON to let a side win at the Victory Threshold (or by eliminating the other), which ends the war and makes peace. Default: off (endless). This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.
Momentum lead one side needs to win the war outright. Default 500.
Momentum gains are multiplied by this when your party takes part in the event. Default 1.5.
When on, the war cannot end until you have fought in enough momentum events yourself. Default: on.
How many battles/sieges you must take part in before either side can win. Default 5.

Gives AI kingdoms that have lost a large share of their towns and castles a small, temporary boost: a higher daily volunteer roll in their towns, castles and villages (empty recruit slots fill faster and waiting recruits are promoted sooner) and faster escapes for their captured lords. Never applies to a kingdom you rule, or to your own clan's settlements and lords; its lords in your prisons escape faster too. Takes effect at the next daily tick; turning it off removes every rally effect. Default on.

Scales every War of the Ring catch-up and event effect (a higher daily volunteer roll, which fills recruit slots faster and promotes waiting recruits sooner; faster escapes of captured lords). 0 turns them off, 1 is the authored size, 2 doubles it. Default 1.

When on, great deeds against the enemy draw a hunter: a Free player is hunted by one of the Nine with a host of Mordor (of Dol Guldur for its four wraiths), an Evil player by Glorfindel with a host of the Eldar. Only while your kingdom is at war with the hunter's. Single-player only. Default: on. This is the default for new campaigns: each campaign keeps its own choice from the start screen, and older saves follow this setting.
Deed score that draws a hunt. A victory over an enemy kingdom in the field, a village raid or a forced levy scores 1, a sally or a battle outside a siege 2, a siege assault 3. Default 10.
Days for the deed score to fall by half. Default 30.
Days after a hunt ends before another can start. Default 60.
Days a hunt lasts before the hunter gives up. Default 20.
Once the hunter is within one and a half times your seeing range, it moves at least this many times your speed. Default 1.3.
The hunter's host is filled to this many times your strength (your army's, when you lead one). Default 1.3.
The most men the hunter's party holds after its host is topped up. Default 250.
The farthest the hunter closes in one hour while out of your sight, in map units. Default 15.

Runs the War Chronicle: lore events of the War of the Ring at set points, and the great sieges (Helm's Deep, Osgiliath, Minas Tirith and others) as timed windows whose result gives both sides small, temporary effects. Off stops new events and clears the army focus; the saved progress is kept. Default on.
Shows a popup on the campaign map when a chronicle event happens, a siege window opens, or a siege is decided. Off keeps the events running silently. Default on.

During a siege window, how much more the attackers' armies want to besiege the target and the defender's armies want to defend it once it is attacked. 1 turns the focus off. Needs AI Strategic Intelligence on. Default 1.4.
Enables configurable T7-T10 troop power values for battle simulation.
If enabled, battle_balance_config.json TierPower values replace the vanilla formula for T1-T6.
Base simulation power for T7 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 3.06).
Base simulation power for T8 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 3.60).
Base simulation power for T9 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 4.18).
Base simulation power for T10 troops (vanilla formula extrapolation = 4.80).
Multiplier applied to heroes in battle simulation. Vanilla = 1.5.
Multiplier applied to mounted troops in battle simulation. Vanilla = 1.2.
Enables configurable wound/kill ratios for battle simulation.
Blunt (wound-only) damage chance in player battles. Vanilla = 0.30.
Blunt damage chance in AI vs AI battles. Vanilla = 0.10.
Applies the per-culture survival modifiers from battle_balance_config.json. A positive value means more of that culture's wounded survive.
When enabled, you receive an event when a watched faction's settlement is besieged, with a timed window to help defend.
Number of in-game days to travel to a besieged settlement before the event expires.
When enabled, AI armies stick to their current target rather than re-optimising every 3 hours. Reduces army thrashing and improves siege follow-through.
How strongly an army commits to its current target. 4.0 = the alternative must score 4x better before the army will divert. Vanilla implicit = 1.3.
Score multiplier applied to the first settlement in a faction's priority list. Decays linearly to 1.0 at the last entry. Affects Mordor, Isengard etc.
Global multiplier applied to all per-faction strength inflation values from army_targeting.json. 1.0 = use JSON defaults. Raise to make evil factions siege even when outnumbered.
Minimum border-proximity score substituted for priority-list targets that vanilla rejects as out-of-range, and only for targets inside the march radius below. 0 = vanilla.
When enabled, kingdoms favour enemies on their own front. Gondor prefers Mordor and Isengard over far northern targets. Weighting only: no war is ever forbidden.

How far, in average town gaps, a priority-list target may be and still have its unreachable verdict overturned by the Border Proximity Floor above. Not a general distance penalty: the game already applies one of its own. 3.2 clears the widest real front on the map.
Score multiplier on defending one of your own settlements. Raise it if AI kingdoms keep besieging abroad while their own fiefs fall. 1.0 = vanilla.

When an AI army of a Free realm takes a town or castle by siege, it stays inside for about 22 hours (12 to 30: longer for a Calculating lord, shorter for a Valorous one) instead of the 10 the game gives. It leaves early if the fortress is besieged, its cohesion drops below 40 or it has less than a day of food, but holds are not saved: after loading a save a running hold cannot end early and runs to its end. Mordor's armies hold too; other Evil realms and (by default) Neutral ones keep rolling on. Single-player only. Needs AI Strategic Intelligence on. Default: on.
Speed multiplier for fast-forward: the map bar fast-forward button, and the fast-forward key (Space by default; rebind under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Default: 4.

Speed multiplier for extra fast-forward: the map bar Extra Fast Forward button (the fourth time button), and the extra fast-forward key (E by default, which is also Rotate Camera Right; rebind either under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Never below the Fast Forward Multiplier. Default: 8.
Speed multiplier while holding Ctrl and the turbo key (Space by default; rebind under Options > Keybindings > Campaign Map). Releases back to prior speed on key-up. Default: 16.
Master toggle for the siege auto-dismount feature. When off, sieges behave vanilla (mount stays equipped).

0 = Vanilla (no change). 1 = RESERVED (currently equivalent to Vanilla — full implementation deferred; would spawn the horse on the map separately). 2 = Mount moves to inventory for siege duration; player must re-equip manually after. 3 = Mount moves to inventory and is auto-restored after siege ends. Default: 3.
Show diagnostic [SiegeDismount] messages on the in-game HUD. Off = file log only.

Before an assault, or before defending a siege, open the 'Manage Troops' screen the lord's hall fight uses and choose who fights. By default, trolls start unticked; tick them to bring them. Troops you leave out take no part in the battle and suffer no losses in it. Takes effect from the next assault. As defender, pressing Escape in the battle surrenders the siege and everyone with it, reserves included. When off, every troop fights as in vanilla. Default: on.
Trolls Stay Off Siege Ladders, Towers and Walls

In a wall battle, trolls never use siege ladders, towers or siege engines. Attacking trolls break the gate down instead, and defending trolls hold the ground behind it and stay off the walls while the AI commands them; a formation you give orders to obeys them. Takes effect from the next battle. When off, trolls behave as in vanilla. Default: on.
Log why rock piles and arrow barrels can or cannot be used in the current mission. Diagnostic only — changes no gameplay. Off by default.
Log every prop, including working ones. Off = log only props that are unusable, plus the summary.

Write the war elephant howdah's and the mumakil war tower's diagnostics to the TAOM log: why a rider did or did not get a howdah, each platform's layout and floor clearance over its beast, a status line every 5 seconds per platform (beast speed against its walking speed, platform drift, how many archers are seated and how many can reach a target) and a battle summary. Diagnostic only, changes no gameplay. On by default while the platforms are being tested.

Serve as a soldier in a lord's party — enlist, take a rank, draw wages, follow the column into battle. Turn OFF to remove the feature: the option to enlist disappears, and if you are already serving you are released honourably (you keep your pay and your gear) rather than being left parked on the map. Takes effect within three in-game hours (in a battle, once it ends); no restart. Default ON.
Offer Leave When The Column Halts

When your company stops at a town, castle or village, ask whether you want a few hours to yourself. The popup exists because the wait menu runs at full speed: a lord's stop is a few campaign hours, which is about two real seconds, and the 'Take leave in the settlement' menu option appears and vanishes inside it. Turn this off and that menu option still works. Takes effect immediately; no restart. Default ON.

Off by default: turn it on to record the routine enlistment trace ([EnlistDiag] TICK, SYNC ok, PARK ok, RESTORE ok) in the TAOM debug log when you are reproducing an enlistment problem for a bug report. It is roughly ten times the volume of the ordinary enlistment log, so turn it off again afterwards. Real faults are always logged regardless of this setting, so [EnlistDiag] lines still appear for them when it is off. Takes effect immediately; no restart.

Soldiers who do the killing in a hard-won battle can be promoted into named companions. Turn OFF to stop it entirely: no merit is earned, no promotion is ever offered. Companions you already promoted stay exactly as they are, and banked merit is kept in case you turn it back on. Takes effect immediately; no restart. Default ON.

The most promotion prompts a single won battle may raise. Each prompt pauses the game, so a large number after a large battle means a long queue of dialogs. Merit above the cap is not lost — it carries to the next battle. Default: 2. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

How outnumbered you must be for a battle to count. Your party's healthy troops divided by the whole enemy side must come in UNDER this. 1.00 = only fights where you are outnumbered; higher = easier fights still earn merit. Default: 1.30.
Merit a troop type banks for each enemy its soldiers kill in a qualifying battle. Higher = faster promotions. Default: 1.

Merit a troop type must bank before it earns a promotion offer. Note merit is pooled per troop TYPE, not per soldier — a large stack of one type reaches the bar faster than a small one. Higher = rarer promotions. Default: 32. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
How many promoted companions you may take beyond your clan tier's companion limit. 0 = the limit is strict and an offer waits until you have room. Default: 0.

Write a detailed [FieldCommission] trace to the TAOM debug log — which battles counted, which troops earned merit, which offers were raised, and every completed promotion. Turn this on before reproducing a promotion problem so the log you send answers it. Real faults are logged regardless of this setting. Off by default.

Send paid messengers to heroes. The price grows with distance. They travel for several days and trigger a conversation on arrival. Disable to grey out the encyclopedia button and stop the dialog line.

Denar price of the shortest trip. The price grows with the distance to the target, and is higher again when the target is at war with you, when you have never met them, and when they sit in a besieged town or castle. A stranger costs more but is never refused. The per-day rate and the multipliers live in messenger_config.json.
In-game days a messenger spends in transit before arriving at the target. Speed scales to map size. The days also scale the price.
Random ambush chance during travel. The base hourly probability lives in messenger_config.json (default 0.2%).
Master toggle. When off, formations use vanilla positioning. When on, formations with mixed melee + ranged units are reordered per the chosen layout while holding position.

Default layout auto-applied to mixed-class formations (>=5 minority units AND >=20% minority share AND >=10 total units). 0=Infantry front + Ranged back. 1=Ranged front + Infantry back. 2=Ranged on the wings, Infantry in the center. 3=Checkerboard. Default: 0.
Bannerlord InputKey name. Pressing this while a formation is selected cycles its layout to the next; pressing while no formation is selected cycles all formations. Default: L.
Writes two diagnostic lines, the auto-assigned default layout and the cycled layout, to the TAOM log file. Nothing is shown on the HUD.
Master toggle. When off, the F6 hotkey and the Fiefs button on the map bar are inert and the carousel options are disabled. Effective immediately at runtime. Default: true.
When on, you can manage any owned fief from anywhere via F6 or the Fiefs button on the map bar. When off, the Manage option is disabled unless you are physically at the selected fief. Default: true.
Write diagnostic [FiefManagement] messages to the TAOM file log. Off = silent.

A Postern Gate (a Hidden Door, Culvert, Sally Port, Hidden Way or Bolt-Hole, by culture) in a besieged fief cuts the troops lost breaking into or out of the siege there: by default 50, 67 and 75 percent by building level (postern_gate.json). When off, the building still exists but the cut does not apply. Takes effect at the next break-in or break-out. Default: on.

Lets your company rebuild a looted village of your own realm from the village menu, and lend its labour to a construction project in a fief you own from the keep menu (from_the_ashes.json holds the hours, labour and materials). When off, those two options are hidden; a job already under way still finishes or stops normally. Single-player only. Default: on.

On the town management window: the fief's name as the title, a Profit row with a daily breakdown, a Patrol row for towns, and tooltips on the stash and prison icons. When off, the title, rows and icons are vanilla; the step buttons have their own switch. Applies the next time the window opens. Default: on.

Adds a button beside the reserve's plus button to put gold into the reserve in one click, and one to take a step back out, refunded in full with no penalty. Single-player only. Applies the next time the window opens. Default: on.

Lets the ruler of your realm rename its towns, castles and villages from the Fiefs tab of the kingdom screen for influence, and lets four fiefs take an older or darker name while the matching side holds them. A name you chose is never overwritten. Single-player only. Switching it off gives those fiefs their map names back; a name you chose stays. The button follows the next time the kingdom screen opens; the older names change at the next capture, load or change of realm. Default: on.

Lets you talk to the governor of a town or castle your clan owns, inside that fief, and pay silver to the watch to raise its loyalty. Each offer shows its price, and there is a ceiling on how far silver can raise loyalty. When off, the line is hidden. Single-player only. Default: on.

A lord's hall shows only as many lords as it has places for, instead of packing every lord in the town or castle onto one spot. The settlement's owner, the ruler, the governor, your own clan, quest givers and the lord you open a conversation with from the town menu always appear; the other places go to the owner's clan first, then clan leaders, then the strongest clans. The lords left out are still in the settlement. Takes effect from the next visit. Default: on.
Master toggle. When off, inventory 'Sell All' uses vanilla. When on, it opens a 4-option menu.
Inventory search box visibility; persists per save and reconciles to MCM each campaign frame.
Items at or below this damage level are sold. Pristine = unused (sentinel). Default: Moderate (-20%).
Custom threshold. Only used when 'Use Custom Threshold' is on. Default: -0.20.
Toggle dropdown vs custom value above.
Skip horses/mounts when selling damaged. Default: true.
Items at or below this denars value are sold. Default: 100.
Ask for confirmation before bulk-selling. Default: true.
Play 'event:/ui/transfer' chime after each batch action. Default: true.
Show diagnostic [QuickActions] HUD messages. Off = file log only.
Master toggle. When off, the Presets overlay is not added to the inventory screen and existing presets are inert (preserved in save).
Maximum saved presets per hero. Default: 10.
Show diagnostic [EquipPresets] messages on the in-game HUD. Off = file log only.

Master toggle. When off, cavalry uses vanilla charge logic. When on, the player's cavalry formations execute coordinated line charges with passthrough + reform behavior. Default OFF while war-elephant interaction is being tuned. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
When charging, cavalry will reroute around friendly infantry on the charge line. Off = vanilla collision behavior (cavalry trample friendly).

How close riders must be to their slots before the line charges, and before a reform counts as done: the average rider may be 10 m off at 0, 4.4 m at the 0.7 default, 2 m at 1. Max Line-Up Seconds launches the charge regardless when it runs out.
Meters past the target before cavalry reforms a new line. Larger = wider passthrough sweep. Default 25.
Multiplier on default unit spacing during line formation. 1.0 = vanilla. 1.2 (default) = slightly wider line for cleaner charge.
Longest the cavalry spend lining up before they charge anyway, and before they re-charge after a reform. Lower is snappier with a looser line. Default 4.
Also write every intercepted charge order and the state it produced to the TAOM log file. State transitions are logged regardless. Nothing is drawn on the HUD.

Each culture's AI fights field battles with its own doctrine: Dwarves hold a shield wall on the high ground, Elves ring their archers with infantry, Rohan leads with cavalry, Mordor and Gundabad mass their infantry. Replaces the tactic list the engine's team AI chooses from; the AI still picks by weight every 5 seconds. Applies from the NEXT battle (the list cannot change once a battle has started). Your own orders are never touched; when you delegate command (F6) your army fights with its culture's doctrine. Off by default until the in-game A/B passes; tuning lives in ModuleData/culture_doctrine/culture_doctrines.json, which reloads on game restart only.

Write a [Doctrine] status line to the TAOM log every 5 seconds of battle time: each team's current tactic and every formation's active behaviour and arrangement. The console command taom.tactic_status prints the same line on demand. Nothing is drawn on the HUD.

Each culture's soldiers hold under fear their own way: Dwarves, Elves, Isengard, Gundabad and Dol Guldur never rout (pride, or a hatred too great), the free peoples of Rohan, Gondor and Dale and the men of the East and South break as vanilla does, and every culture carries a bravery offset on its starting morale. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

Each culture's soldiers fight the melee their own way: orcs attack on sight and rarely cover with a shield, Dwarves and Gondor raise shields and hold, Elves shoot straighter, Rohan commits to a charge from further out. Multiplies the engine's per-soldier AI decision values after skill has set them. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies to soldiers spawned from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

Dwarves, Isengard and Dale, defending outnumbered against an army of mostly horse, stand where horse cannot ride them down: a choke point, a forest, a slope, or where they are. Where the riders sit on ordinary horses, the cavalry dismount and join the shield wall with polearms ready. The AI sides only; your own army is never touched. Needs Enable Culture Doctrine. Applies from the next battle; tuning in culture_doctrines.json.

Remove killed horses, wargs and other mounts a few seconds after they die instead of leaving them on the field. A mount is a full agent with a skeleton and a live ragdoll, so a cavalry battle piles up corpses that cost frame time and do nothing. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs only; towns, arenas and tournaments keep their bodies. Side effect: freeing agent slots lets reinforcements arrive slightly sooner than vanilla.
Seconds between a mount's death and its fade. Default 5. Below 3 the corpse pops while the death animation is still playing, so values outside 3-30 fall back to 5.

Fade fallen soldiers after a set time and cap how many bodies a battle keeps, whatever your Number of Corpses option says. The engine walks its whole corpse list every frame, and players reported mid-battle freezes at high corpse settings. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs only; towns, arenas and hideouts keep their bodies. Never raises your own Number of Corpses option.

Seconds a body stays on the field, counted from when it settles, before it fades. Default 60. The engine's own default is an hour, so without this a body only goes when the corpse cap pushes it out. Values outside 10-300 fall back to 60.
Most bodies a battle keeps at once; the oldest fade first. Default 25, the vanilla Low setting. If your own Number of Corpses option is lower, yours is used.
On the first main menu after the game starts, offer to lower Number of Ragdolls to 5 and Number of Corpses to Low when yours are higher. Nothing changes unless you click Apply.
Lower Number of Ragdolls to 5 and Number of Corpses to Low (25) in your game options now. A setting already lower is kept. Change them back at any time in Options, Performance.
Append detected combat role (e.g., [BOW], [INF]) to companion/troop tooltips on the party screen.
Show role indicators on hero items in the Order of Battle screen.
Show diagnostic [CompanionRoles] messages on the in-game HUD.

Presets save and load the formation types, captains and hero troops of the Order of Battle, per campaign. Off by default until it is checked in game; opt in to try it. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.
Maximum saved formation presets per campaign. Save attempts beyond this limit are refused with a warning. Default: 10.

Parked: show a bar of stance buttons during field battles. The buttons record a stance but do not change formation behavior yet, and they can be clicked only while a menu shows the cursor (for example Esc). Default: off.
Auto-clear stance when the formation receives a movement order.
Include 'Volley Fire' as a ranged action option.

Master toggle. When off, hideout density + bandit party sizes use vanilla values. When on, both scale with PlayerProgress (0.0 new campaign -> 1.0 endgame) per the curves below. Turning it off restores vanilla's live numbers at once (including its 2-party minimum for a camp to count as infested) and stops scaling future spawns; it deletes no bandit party already on the map and culls no hideout above the cap, so a swamped campaign thins only as they are cleared.

Multiplier on hideout count + parties-per-hideout at PlayerProgress=1.0. Curve: 1 + curve * progress. 0 = vanilla density throughout. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x density in endgame. Both caps below bind first.

Multiplier on bandit party troop counts at PlayerProgress=1.0. Vanilla already scales 0.4 -> 1.2; this is a final multiplier on top. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x bandit party sizes in endgame. Each troop stack is capped at its party template's max_value, which binds before 2.5x is reached.

Multiplier on the FIRST fight's troop count inside hideouts at PlayerProgress=1.0. 1.5 (default) = up to 2.5x bandits in the camp-clearing phase of a hideout assault in endgame. The boss fight is not scaled: it is exactly the boss plus Hideout Boss Bodyguards below.
Hard cap on hideouts per bandit faction regardless of scaling curve. Vanilla = 9. Default: 100 (effectively the physical hideout count per faction).

Hard cap on bandit parties per hideout regardless of scaling curve. Vanilla = 3, which is also the floor: a cap at or below 3 pins the value at vanilla and the Density Curve cannot move it. Default: 6. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Hideouts each bandit faction starts with on a NEW campaign; read once at world-gen, so changing it does nothing to a campaign already in progress. TAOM has 8 bandit factions, so this is a per-faction target, x8 on the map, bounded by each faction's physical hideout count (three have only 10). Vanilla = 7. Default: 7. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Soldiers standing with the hideout boss in the final fight, on both the daytime assault and the night sneak-in. The fight is exactly the boss plus this many (0 = the boss alone), whether you take the duel or fight them all; the rest of the camp is cleared in the first phase. Applies with Enable Bandit Scaling off too. Vanilla fields 5 to 10 with the boss. Default: 4.

When enabled, a recruiter cannot recruit volunteers at a settlement controlled by an opposed-alignment kingdom (Free vs Evil). Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json, keyed by the kingdom you serve. Neutral factions (Umbar etc.) never block. When off, recruitment is vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

When ON, only a Free-aligned recruiter is blocked from Evil-controlled settlements; Evil recruiters may recruit anywhere, and Alignment Desertion then removes no Free troops from Evil lords or their garrisons at all, not only the ones they recruit. When OFF (default), the block is symmetric: Free and Evil each refuse the other, and opposed troops desert either way.

When ON (default), YOU are blocked from recruiting in opposed-alignment settlements. When OFF, you may recruit anyone regardless of alignment (AI lords are still gated if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on). The master 'Enable Recruitment Alignment Block' toggle off disables the whole feature for everyone.
When ON (default), AI lords are also blocked from recruiting in opposed-alignment settlements. When OFF, AI recruits freely (you are still gated if 'Apply To Player' is on).

When enabled, a Free-aligned hero cannot marry an Evil-aligned one (no Gondorian weds an orc). Alignment comes from execution/alignment.json, keyed by the hero's CULTURE. Neutral cultures (Khand, Umbar, Shaghana, Abanissa) marry anyone; Dunland is Evil. When off, marriage is vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.

When ON (default), YOUR clan is also held to the rule — you and your siblings/children cannot marry across the Free/Evil line. When OFF, the player clan marries freely (AI lords are still gated if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on).
When ON (default), AI lords are blocked from marrying across the Free/Evil line. When OFF, AI marries freely (you are still gated if 'Apply To Player' is on).

When ON (default), AI lords look for a partner among compatible clans instead of drawing uniformly from every clan in the world. Vanilla's draw wastes the day whenever it lands on a blocked clan, which would make Free factions (Gondor, Rohan, Dale) marry far less often and run short of heirs. Turn OFF to keep the block but restore vanilla's draw.

When enabled, a wanderer will not take service across the Free/Evil line: Free-culture wanderers (Gondor, Rohan, the Elves, Erebor and the rest) refuse a player who serves Sauron, and Evil-culture wanderers refuse a player on the Free side. Your side is the kingdom you serve (execution/alignment.json), falling back to your clan's culture when you serve no kingdom. Neutral cultures serve anyone and a Neutral player is refused by nobody. Companions already in your clan are never affected. When off, hiring is vanilla.

All wanderers (default): every wanderer, by culture. Named companions only: just the lore characters from named_companions.xml (Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli and the rest); generic tavern wanderers hire as in vanilla.

When enabled, a lord held prisoner by your clan (in your party or in one of your settlements) can be questioned about his clan's or kingdom's lands, for a bribe or by force, and stripped of his arms and armour. Force and stripping cost relation, Honor and Mercy, and stripping costs renown. Each topic works once per captivity. When off, those conversation options do not appear.

When enabled, a conversation with a lord who leads a party offers a line to gift him troops through a donate-style party screen. The lord must not be in your clan or kingdom, not at war with you, and not on the opposite side of the Free/Evil divide (a Neutral lord may receive). Troops move from you to him only. The gift is paid by Bonds of Battle's hand-over rule (half the influence the gift is worth, at most 10 relation a day per relation owner), so the relation needs Bonds of Battle and its Troop Gifts Win Lords' Favour switch on; with either off the gift is still accepted but earns nothing. When off, the line does not appear.

When enabled, you can ask a free lord about his clan's holdings. A lord who knows you well enough names them and they are marked on your map; a lord who does not refuses, and a lord whose clan holds nothing says so, each at a small cost in relation. Lords at war with you and your own clan never answer. When off, the line does not appear.

When enabled, a notable of the settlement you stand in (an artisan, gang leader, merchant, rural notable or headman, but not a preacher) offers three lines in conversation: give men to the settlement (troops raise its militia, prisoners its hearth in a village or its prosperity in a town; a castle takes troops only), pay to be introduced to the other notables there, and pay to have the nearest towns and castles marked on your map. Single player only; all three lines are hidden during a messenger conversation. At war with the settlement's realm only the gift line is hidden: the introduction still works and the holds question is refused. The gift line is also hidden while a party screen is open or when you hold no regular troop or prisoner. Amounts are in notable_services.json. When off, none of the lines appear. Default: on.

When enabled, if you attack on land a bandit party you have not dealt with before and it belongs to one of the eight talking clans (Dunlending, Rhun, Haradrim, Gundabad, Umbar, Gondor deserters, Blacklocks, Mirkwood Stalkers), there is a one in four chance that it greets you in its own words, and your ultimatum is vanilla's reply to that kind of greeting. With Encounter Lines also on, these clans greet you in a line chosen by your people and your side on half of these meetings, and keep vanilla's greeting on the other quarter. Feral Orcs and looters, which have no greetings of their own, greet you that way on three meetings in four. Spiders and wild trolls are unchanged. Applies to the next bandit conversation. Text only: nothing else about the encounter changes. When off, every greeting is vanilla's. The lines bandits use when they rob you are separate data; with Encounter Lines on, half of these robberies use its lines instead. Default: on.

When enabled, lords you meet on the map speak in the voice of their people and by who you are to them: their liege, an ally, a rival, a foe, or one of their own. Caravans and villagers greet you this way half of the time on a first meeting on land, and speak their own words when they surrender to a robbery. Bandit clans rob you with their own threats, and a hideout boss challenges you in the clan's own words. Bandit greetings when you attack a bandit party also need Enable Bandit Clan Greetings (World/Bandit Voices) on. Lords in your clan, companions, wanderers and notables keep vanilla's lines, and so do lords you speak to inside a settlement; the hideout boss still speaks the clan's own words.
